title: Music longer than the edit stops where the picture stops
goal: Put a three minute song under a ninety second cut and the whole edit becomes three minutes long: the title bar, the timeline and the Export sheet all say 2:59, and the exported MP4 is ninety seconds of talk followed by ninety seconds of song over a blank picture. Nothing on screen points this out. A music bed is in the focus workflow, and a person who has just cut to ninety seconds expects ninety seconds out. A song that runs past the last picture stops where the picture stops (settled on 2026-10-20, when the waiting cards were taken as recommended).
notes: Reproduced 2026-10-08 by the manager: /tmp/mgr-walks2/music-bed.json (the-ninety-second-cut-walk steps, then importPicks a 180 s m4a made with ffmpeg sine, Sequence > Add Media at Playhead at 0:00). Result: step 62 expectTimeline: the timeline runs 179975ms, not 90000ms. Pictures: queue/manager/shots/2026-10-08-0640-music-past-the-cut.png (title bar Long Talk Retina 2880 x 1800 2:59, Song on Audio 2 to 3:00, V1 ends at 1:30) and queue/manager/shots/2026-10-08-0640-export-says-2-59.png (sheet line 2880 x 1800 px 30 fps 2:59). Code: EditorState+Audio.swift addSound(from:atMS:) lands the whole sound; the document length is the latest end of any layer. Premiere does the same (sequence runs to the end of the longest track); iMovie and Clips trim background music to the movie. Related but separate: music-dips-under-the-speech-by-itself (ducking, its own card).
acceptance: A song longer than the edit stops with the last picture: the title bar, the timeline and the Export sheet say the length of the picture, and the MP4 ends there, at Next defaults with no switch

A walk (music-bed-under-a-cut-walk or similar) opens the five minute talk, cuts it to ninety seconds as the-ninety-second-cut-walk does, adds a sound longer than the edit with Sequence > Add Media at Playhead at 0:00, and checks the timeline length and the Export sheet say what the answer promises; it also drops the sound on the timeline by dragging and gets the same result
A sound shorter than the edit, and a sound added on its own with no picture at all, behave exactly as today
One Undo takes the landing back whole

Adversarial pass before building: a Premiere editor expects the sequence to run to the longest track, an iMovie/Clips user expects the music trimmed to the movie; the card settled on the iMovie answer. Risk found: ~14 walks and 13 core tests used the 14 s sample song on the 8 s sample recording as a fixture for other features (box picks, level lines, holds), so they relied on music running past the picture.

Chose: one rule in core (PhotonzDocument.soundLengthUnderThePicture) used by addSound and by the timeline drop/place-at-playhead landing, over trimming inside clipLanding, because clipLanding also serves Paste and a pasted clip should keep its length. Picture = any timed layer that is not sound-only, plus the written length where the video holds past its last clip. A sound put down at or after the picture's end, or in a video with no picture, lands whole as before. The rest of the song stays in the clip (sourceLengthMS), so dragging its end out brings it back.

Chose to keep the old fixtures meaning what they meant over rewriting their geometry: core addSound gained stoppingWithThePicture: false (13 fixture calls use it) and walks gained the action soundAddSampleWhole (12 walks switched). captionsAddVoiceover lays its voiceover whole, since every sentence is what captioning walks count on. playback-speed-walk presses Home before 4x because its 12 s tone now stops at 0:08.

Looked at the audit pictures: 1 (song on Audio 0:00 to 1:30, title bar and transport 1:30), 2 (Export sheet line 2880 x 1800 px · 30 fps · 1:30), 3 (dropped song stops at 1:30).
